key_insight: A frozen gastrointestinal foundation model’s patch features can be turned into compact, human-readable fuzzy rules by clustering prototype similarities, revealing how latent space encodes clinically relevant patterns.
clinical_relevance: This offers a transparent way to interpret endoscopy and polyp representations, potentially helping clinicians and researchers understand model decisions and assess synthetic images more clearly.
method: Extract patch-level features from the final two blocks of frozen ViT-S/16 backbones.
Learn class-specific prototypes by clustering in feature space.
Classify using fuzzy IF-THEN rules over prototype-similarity scores, without backbone fine-tuning.
evidence_signal: The approach was benchmarked on wireless capsule endoscopy, gastrointestinal endoscopy, and colonic polyp segmentation, and achieved accuracy comparable to kNN, kernel SVM, and linear probing on the same frozen features.
watch_item: Interpretability depends on the quality and stability of learned prototypes, so results may vary with dataset shift, clustering choices, and the backbone’s pretraining domain.
paper_title: From Image Latent Space to Fuzzy Rules: Interpretable Analysis of Gastrointestinal Foundation Model
